picks.title: ARIA and PPCA launch 'Not AI's to Take' campaign for permission-first AI copyright rules in Australia
picks.rationale: New organised action: Australia's recording bodies ARIA and PPCA formally launch a cross-sector campaign that asks Canberra to reject an opt-out TDM exception and require consent before training. The 11-09 Guardian card was only IFPI's warning.
picks.excerpt: Australia's recording-industry bodies ARIA and PPCA lead a cross-sector campaign urging Canberra to reject an opt-out text-and-data-mining exception and require AI companies to obtain consent before training on music and other creative works.

picks.title: Elvis Presley Enterprises and Authentic Brands Group file amended, expanded Suno copyright and NIL suit
picks.rationale: New court filing: an amended complaint that adds claims to the Elvis estate's Suno suit, which matters for voice and likeness rights in AI music. It is the single Suno-litigation card allowed today.
picks.excerpt: Elvis Presley Enterprises, Authentic Brands Group and co-plaintiffs have filed an amended and expanded infringement and name-and-likeness complaint against AI music generator Suno, adding new claims.

picks.title: Initial Audio updates Difro Melody AI to v2.5 with local audio-to-MIDI and a VST3/AU plugin
picks.rationale: Producers can use it right away. The new version adds local audio-to-MIDI conversion (loops up to 16 bars) and a VST3/AU plugin with DAW sync, and it has a free tier.
picks.excerpt: Difro Melody AI 2.5 converts dragged-in melodic loops of up to 16 bars to MIDI locally, then generates variations with Re-Imagine; it now runs as a VST3/AU plugin with DAW sync and realtime MIDI/audio output. Free tier with limited generations, Pro unlimited.

picks.title: Kanye West's Bully up for Best Rap Album Grammy despite A.I. allegations
picks.rationale: New event: an album dogged by AI-use allegations got a 2027 Grammy nomination, which tests the Recording Academy's AI eligibility line. Pitchfork was kept over Consequence (same cluster c2) for outlet spread.
picks.excerpt: Widespread allegations of A.I. use did not deter Grammy voters from nominating Ye's critically dismissed LP Bully for Best Rap Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

picks.title: AI music used in Somerset carnival processions 'disappointing'
picks.rationale: A grassroots example of AI music replacing local musicians: clubs at Bridgwater Carnival, the UK's oldest, soundtracked their illuminated carts with AI tracks, and opinion was divided. It is a fresh story from a credible outlet.
picks.excerpt: Some clubs at Bridgwater Carnival, the UK's oldest, soundtracked their illuminated carts with AI-generated music, dividing opinion among local musicians and carnival-goers.

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates: Consequence's Kanye 'Bully' Grammy item (same cluster c2 as the Pitchfork pick). Engadget 'Vibe coding is changing how musicians customize their gear' (same trend feature as the Verge 10-20 card and the 10-29 Akai/Behringer cards; also dropped 11-16). diginomica on UMG's CEO and AI slop (commentary, same theme as the musically 11-02 'UMG talks AI music' card). Skipped under the brief's limit of 1 Suno-litigation card (not a duplicate): UMG v. Suno II stay/discovery dispute (DMN). Skipped on score or scope: Matt Bellamy AI-guitar interview (opinion), Chosun ALS singer BCI voice (closer to science/medicine than music), and the arXiv MusicRWKV and creativity-evaluation papers (title-only excerpts, no abstract read). Cross-section: per the curator brief, 'Not AI's to Take' is assigned to music only. Outlets: Australasian Leisure Management, Digital Music News, KVR Audio, Pitchfork, BBC News (5 distinct; 1 per outlet).
